mainEntity.name: What are the main factors that decide Google Maps ranking?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google says local results are mainly based on relevance, distance and prominence. Relevance is how well your profile matches the search, distance is how far you are from the person searching, and prominence is how well known your business is. Google does not publish a weight for each factor.

mainEntity.name: Can I pay Google to rank higher on Google Maps?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Google states that there is no way to request or pay for a better local ranking. Paid ads are a separate product and do not change the local ranking itself.

mainEntity.name: Do more reviews make me rank higher?

acceptedAnswer.text: Google says more reviews and positive ratings can help your business's local ranking. It does not say by how much. Ask every customer honestly, reply to reviews, and never offer a reward for one.

mainEntity.name: Can I add keywords to my business name to rank higher?

acceptedAnswer.text: No. Google's guidelines say that including unnecessary information in your business name isn't permitted and can lead to suspension. Use the name customers see on your sign and your invoices.

mainEntity.name: Why does my ranking change depending on where I search from?

acceptedAnswer.text: Because distance is measured from the person searching. You can rank well near your location and lower in other neighborhoods, and no setting changes that.
